title: Defective Chromatic Polynomials: the closed form for the linear-forest counts of two cospectral tree families (Lemma 5.2)
author: Shamil Asgarli, Tamsen Whitehead McGinley, Nicholas Xue
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's expansion of the defective chromatic polynomial into linear forests, printed as Lemma 5.9 (source0.tex lines 602-614) and delivered with the paper's own complete 77-line proof (lines 616-692). The statement expresses the defective chromatic polynomial of a graph as a sum over linear forests with weights that record the defect parameters and the components' sizes, which is the structural identity the paper's later results are built on. The proof is the paper's own counting argument: it classifies the proper defective colourings by the monochromatic connected components that the defect allowance permits, shows that those components form a linear forest, counts the colourings of each such forest by inclusion-exclusion over its edges and components, and reassembles the resulting weights into the stated polynomial. This is a research-level graph-polynomial expansion rather than a qualifying-examination exercise; the unit is H2.
